header: Date: 2026-10-06T15:00:00-07:00; Duration: 45m; Attendees: Jordan Mills (Redwood AE), Samira Ko (Redwood SE), Miguel Alvarez (Redwood CSM), Nina Patel (LatticePay VP Eng), Marco Ruiz (LatticePay SRE), Sophie Chen (LatticePay Security)
summary: Follow-up postmortem after 2026-10-04 intermittent outage impacting LatticePay payment authorizations. Discussed root cause (KV cache invalidation + autoscaler behavior causing thundering retries), mitigations applied, permanent fixes (runtime patch + runbook), security/KMS questions, and next steps for benchmarks and runbook rollout.
topics: Root cause review: KV cache invalidation and autoscale interaction
Long-term fixes: runtime patch and canary rollout
Security and compliance: KMS, audit logs, SSO/SAML concerns
Operational runbook updates and testing plan
Benchmarks and regression tests to prevent recurrence
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Mills: Hey everybody, thanks for joining. We wanted to run through the postmortem follow-up from the 10/04 incident. I'll kick off with a super-brief timeline.
[00:18] Nina Patel: Yup, thanks. We're mainly here to make sure the things you patched are sufficient and to get the runbook and SLAs tightened.
[00:28] Samira Ko: Quick reminder - Redwood rolled a mitigation Saturday night, we disabled the aggressive autoscaler rule and applied a hotfix to the KV cache eviction logic. That reduced the retry storms.
[00:42] Marco Ruiz: Right, we saw the error rates drop after that. There was still a couple of spikes, though, around 02:10 UTC. Not as bad but noticeable.
[00:55] Sophie Chen: From security side, we need the redacted traces and confirmation that no PII left logs. Also confirmation on key rotation and KMS usage - we need HSM-backed keys for production.
[01:12] Jordan Mills: On the logs question - yes, we'll send a trimmed set of traces. We'll redact tokens and any card or PII. Jordan: action item to share by Friday.
[01:25] Marco Ruiz: Can you explain the root cause again? My notes say something about KV cache invalidation + autoscaler interplay leading to a cascade.
[01:36] Samira Ko: Yeah, so sequence was: a spike in large sequences caused the runtime's KV cache to reach its eviction threshold; eviction created more cache misses which increased tail latency; the autoscaler heuristic interpreted tail latency as under-provisioning and spun up new pods, which triggered more cold-starts and repeated KV cache misses - creating a feedback loop. There was also a bug in how the autoscaler backoff was calculated - the cooldown wasn't honored in one path.
[02:05] Nina Patel: So autoscaler created the problem and also made it worse.
[02:09] Samira Ko: Exactly. It was both the cache invalidation and the cooldown bug. The autoscaler amplified the effect.
[02:18] Marco Ruiz: That matches what we saw. We had an initial 2-3 minute blip, then a large number of retries from our side because our client SDKs were retrying on 504s. The retries stacked on top.
[02:32] Jordan Mills: That's an important call-out - client-side retry policies contributed. We should coordinate recommended retry/backoff settings.
[02:40] Miguel Alvarez: Quick note - we added tickets to the shared tracker for the retry guidance doc.
[02:46] Sophie Chen: On encryption/KMS: can you confirm where the keys live and whether Redwood does any envelope encryption on your side?
[02:56] Samira Ko: We do customer-specific keys for Private deployments; for hosted we use per-tenant keys stored in our KMS with envelope encryption. For enterprise customers we can integrate with customer-managed KMS/HSM. We will follow up with a security-to-security call next week to validate.
[03:15] Nina Patel: Good. We need that SSO and audit log proof for our compliance team.
[03:22] Jordan Mills: We'll attach SOC2 artifacts and the logs. We'll also show the runbook changes.
[03:27] Marco Ruiz: What was the immediate mitigation timeline? I have that you rolled a hotfix at 22:45 UTC on 10/04?
[03:35] Samira Ko: Close - we started mitigation 22:38 UTC, hotfix to KV eviction at 22:45, and the autoscaler rule disabled at 22:50. Full steady-state around 23:20 UTC.
[03:49] Nina Patel: Can you explain the hotfix - was it a config change or code?
[03:54] Samira Ko: It was a small runtime patch: we adjusted the eviction window to use a frequency-aware policy and added a short-lived in-memory grace cache for recently-evicted KV entries. That plus disabling the autoscaler path stopped the cascade.
[04:11] Marco Ruiz: Are those fixes permanent? We don't want the patch to regress or cause memory growth.
[04:18] Samira Ko: The hotfix is temporary; there's a proper patch slated that changes cache eviction logic and includes a stable cooldown enforcement for the autoscaler. That patch has unit/integration tests and will be canaried.
[04:30] Jordan Mills: Timeline for the permanent fix?
[04:33] Samira Ko: We're aiming to cut the runtime fix 2026-10-11, run a canary for 48 hours, then full rollout if green - so complete by 2026-10-15 assuming no regressions.
[04:46] Nina Patel: We need a rollback plan and metrics.
[04:49] Samira Ko: Rollback is immediate via config flag; the release is gated with a Health check and latency/error thresholds. We'll share the canary dashboard.
[04:58] Marco Ruiz: On our side, we'll also adjust SDK retry behavior. Our SREs propose increasing initial backoff to 200ms and exponential capped at 2s; we can coordinate on a recommended client setting.
[05:13] Jordan Mills: We'll put that recommended retry policy in the integration docs and include a short code snippet.
[05:18] Miguel Alvarez: Also, runbook updates - who owns the on-call play? Miguel volunteered to draft runbook updates.
[05:24] Miguel Alvarez: Yep I'll draft the steps: detection, mitigation knobs (disable autoscaler rule, enable grace-cache, abort rollout), and escalation matrix.
[05:31] Nina Patel: Please also include communication templates for customers when incidents hit.
[05:35] Miguel Alvarez: Will do.
[05:36] Sophie Chen: A couple security items: we need to confirm audit log retention for 90 days and whether logs are tamper-evident.
[05:45] Samira Ko: Audit logs are immutable in our log archive for hosted customers with enterprise retention. We'll send the retention policy doc.
[05:53] Jordan Mills: Action items recap - Jordan will send traces, Samira will run stress tests and share benchmarks, Miguel will draft runbook, Marco validate client settings.
[06:01] Nina Patel: One more thing - can Redwood run a pre-scheduled chaos test in our staging next week so we can validate the fix end-to-end?
[06:10] Samira Ko: Yes, we can run a KV-cache eviction chaos test and the autoscale stress scenario in your staging on 10/12. We'll coordinate windows.
[06:19] Marco Ruiz: If we schedule on 10/12 we'll need logs and dashboard access.
[06:23] Jordan Mills: We'll give a temporary read-only dashboard access for the run.
[06:27] Sophie Chen: Any regulatory paperwork needed for that access?
[06:30] Miguel Alvarez: We'll use SSO provisioning and scoped API keys; we can do a short IOA and checklist.
[06:38] Nina Patel: Alright, that's good. I want to capture the long term asks: durable fixes, updated runbook, recommended client retry policy, and security validation.
[06:49] Samira Ko: Agreed. We'll put all of this into the ticket tracker and mark dependencies.
[06:54] Jordan Mills: Before we close, quick question about cost/throughput tradeoffs - does the new cache approach increase memory usage?
[07:03] Samira Ko: The planned fix will be memory-neutral overall; the short grace-cache is small and bounded. We will provide estimated memory delta per pod.
[07:14] Marco Ruiz: Also want to understand effects on latency percentiles with the fix - we'll need 99th percentile numbers.
[07:20] Samira Ko: We'll provide P50/P95/P99 from the canary run.
[07:25] Nina Patel: Ok thanks - last ask: please share the ticket links and canary dashboard after the call.
[07:31] Jordan Mills: Will do. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up in writing with the action items and schedule the staging test.
[07:38] END OF TRANSCRIPT
